2: He stood, with high and dread thoughts filled,
3: And gazed afar. Before him rolled
4: The river wide, a fragile bark
6: Upon the moss-grown banks and swamps
8: The homes of Finnish fishers poor;

14: From hence we can the Swede best threat;
15: Here must I found a city strong,
16: That shall our haughty foe bring ill;
17: It is by nature's law decreed,
18: That here we break a window through,
20: And on the sea with sure foot stand;
21: By water path as yet unknown,
22: Shall ships from distant ports arrive,
23: And far ard wide our reign extend.
25: A hundred years have passed, and now,
26: In place of forests dark and swamps,
27: A city new, in pomp unmatched,
28: Of Northern lands the pride and gem.
29: Where Finnish fisher once at eve,
31: From low-sunk boat was wont his net
32: With patient toil to cast, and drag
33: The stream, now stretch long lines of quays,
34: Of richest granite formed, and rows
35: Of buildings huge and lordly domes
37: The river front; whilst laden ships
38: From distant quarters of the world
39: Our hungry wharfs fresh spoils supply;
40: And needful bridge its span extends,
41: To join the stream's opposing shores;
42: And islets gay, in verdure clad,
43: Beneath the shade of gardens laugh.
45: Her head proud Moscow jealous bends,
46: As when the new Tsaritza young
48: I love thee, work of Peter's hand!
50: I love thy stern, symmetric form;
51: The Neva's calm and queenly flow
54: Thy nights so soft with pensive thought,
55: Their moonless glow, in bright obscure,
56: When I alone, in cosy room,
57: Or write or read, night's lamp unlit;
58: The sleeping piles that clear stand out
59: In lonely streets, and needle bright,
62: When, chasing far the shades of night,
63: In cloudless sky of golden pure,
64: Dawn quick usurps the pale twilight,
65: And brings to end her half-hour reign.
66: I love thy winters bleak and harsh;
67: Thy stirless air fast bound by frosts;
68: The flight of sledge o'er Neva wide,
69: That glows the cheeks of maidens gay.
70: I love the noise and chat of balls;
71: A banquet free from wife's control,"
72: Where goblets foam, and bright blue flame
74: Darts round the brimming punch-bowl's edge.
75: I love to watch the martial troops
76: The spacious Field of Mars fast scour;
77: The squadrons spruce of foot and horse;
78: The nicely chosen race of steeds,
79: As gaily housed they stand in line,
80: Whilst o'er them float the tattered flags;
81: The gleaming helmets of the men
82: That bear the marks of battle-shot.
83: I love thee, when with pomp of war
86: When Empress-Queen of all the North
87: Hath given birth to royal heir;
90: Or when her bonds of ice once more
92: The herald sure of spring's rebirth.
93: Fair city of the hero, hail!
94: Like Russia, stand unmoved and firm!
96: Make lasting peace with thee and thine.
